target_customer: Inside sales teams and their managers, mostly US customers
problem: Sales reps get coaching only after calls, too late to change outcomes, and managers cannot listen to every call.

founders.name: Shruti Kapoor
founders.background_notes: Later led Clari's international business after the acquisition.

founders.name: Muralidharan Venkatasubramanian
founders.background_notes: Described as an engineer on the YC page.

competitors.name: Chorus.ai
competitors.what: Listens to and analyzes sales calls, with real-time coaching
competitors.funding_then: US$33M Series B led by Georgian Partners in December 2018, about US$55M total per the press release

competitors.name: Gong
competitors.funding_then: US$20M round in July 2017, extended with Cisco Investments in April 2018

technical_complexity.rationale: Real-time speech transcription and suggestion surfacing used off-the-shelf speech models but needed low-latency engineering and call integrations.

defensibility.rationale: Better funded rivals Gong and Chorus.ai already had the call data and customers; Wingman differentiated on real-time prompts and an India-based cost base.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Clari bought Wingman in June 2022 and renamed it Wingman by Clari, later Clari Copilot.

market_need_then: Gong and Chorus.ai had raised tens of millions by 2018, which shows buyers were paying for sales call analysis at the time of the batch.

brand_strength.rationale: The name evokes a helper during a call, which matches the real-time coaching product, but it is a common word and no source documents brand-driven growth; the brand was folded into Clari's within a few years.

outcome_analysis: Wingman, a Bengaluru team, sold real-time sales call coaching into a market where Gong and Chorus.ai were already funded, reached more than 200 customers by its acquisition, and was bought by Clari in June 2022 for an undisclosed sum, then absorbed into Clari Copilot. The exit looks like a strategic purchase of conversation intelligence rather than a failure; the price is unknown.
notes: The company site trywingman.com returned HTTP 503. The US$2.3M seed rests on Seedtable and an Indian Startup Times profile that gives a lower aggregate for some sources (CB Insights shows US$150K over 3 rounds); investor lists differ (Venture Highway, Speciale Invest, Arali Ventures, VH Capital), so only Y Combinator and Speciale Invest, named across them, are recorded. No press release confirming the round was found. Founder education and prior employers were not found in any opened source. Customer count of more than 200 comes from the Indian Startup Times profile. Competitor traction figures were not recorded.
